perspective:
From Cynthia Huber’s available perspective:

- I am Cynthia Huber, a teacher at the community center where I teach evening classes. Christina Gonzalez is my colleague who manages marketing. We are professional but not close, and we have had disagreements about programs and community engagement.
- At the staff meeting about next semester’s marketing materials, I advocated highlighting traditional classes as the backbone of our success. I heard Christina argue for showcasing dynamic, interactive sessions and innovation. I responded that traditional methods are proven, our core audience values structure and depth, and shifting focus too drastically risks alienating long-time attendees. Christina said it was about enhancing and balancing, not replacing. I was not convinced at that time.
- Later, I saw positive feedback from Christina’s innovative marketing campaign. I approached her and asked what she did differently. She told me she focused on interactive elements and used social media to create conversation rather than just broadcast information. I said I valued depth over flash but that she had captured both. She said blending new and old methods meant we could learn from each other.
- I proposed a joint pilot project combining traditional lectures with interactive online sessions. Christina agreed it could test how well our methods blend. We planned to outline specifics and implementation. I hoped it would enhance learning and draw a wider audience.
- After the pilot succeeded, I wanted to scale it immediately. I said I would organize resources and set up a schedule. Christina said she would coordinate with the marketing team. I was excited about the impact, and Christina said to keep the momentum going.
- I prepared a presentation to showcase the project’s success and advocate expanding it to other centers. I told Christina the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. She offered help and agreed other centers could benefit. I felt proud and saw it as proof that blending our methods was the right move.

I have no access to hidden or private information beyond what I observed, heard, did, or was told in these interactions.
